title: Serotonin Syndrome Versus Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
subject: Pharmacology
preview: Serotonin syndrome often has rapid onset with clonus, hyperreflexia, autonomic activation and agitation.
quickRevision: Serotonin syndrome often has rapid onset with clonus, hyperreflexia, autonomic activation and agitation.
Medication history and neuromuscular findings help distinguish these potentially fatal syndromes.
Stop the offending agents, provide supportive care and escalate based on severity.

sections.title: Pathophysiology & identification
points: Serotonin syndrome often has rapid onset with clonus, hyperreflexia, autonomic activation and agitation.
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome commonly evolves more slowly with marked rigidity, fever and altered mental status after dopamine blockade.

sections.title: Diagnostic and treatment connections
points: Medication history and neuromuscular findings help distinguish these potentially fatal syndromes.
Stop the offending agents, provide supportive care and escalate based on severity.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Hyperreflexia and clonus favor serotonin toxicity; do not use fever alone to differentiate.

quiz.question: Which feature supports serotonin syndrome more than NMS?
quiz.explanation: Clonus and hyperreflexia. Serotonin syndrome often has rapid onset with clonus, hyperreflexia, autonomic activation and agitation.
